articles.detail: 5 cycles completed, avg 10 published/cycle (down from 65 yesterday)

experiment: Skipped — all four goals are met with margin, no experiment was pending evaluation, and no noNewExperimentsUntil gate is set. The day's one real defect (a same-event double-publish, below) sits in scripts/lib/dedup.js layer gating, which is outside the tunable-parameter surface; no feed cap or selector floor would have caught it.
weakestArea: Africa at 4 articles and Oceania at 2 are the thinnest regions, but neither breaches a target — the genuine miss is a same-event double-publish that the duplicates counter reads as zero. The 08:43 cycle shipped 2026-09-08-navier-stokes-blow-up-claim-verification-burden (tech, Quanta Magazine) and the 11:48 cycle shipped 2026-09-08-navier-stokes-ai-assisted-proof-steps-verification (science, New Scientist) — one AI-assisted Navier-Stokes proof claim, two articles, two categories, three hours apart. The URL layer cannot see it because the URLs differ, and the title-overlap layer is gated to niche-only sources, so two mainstream outlets covering one event pass straight through. This is the second consecutive day a duplicate has shipped and the third distinct shape of the same failure: same URL (2026-09-07 ziltivekimab), same title from different clusters (2026-09-06 Lebanon hospital), and now same event under different categories.
watching: The two ziltivekimab articles from 2026-09-07 are still both live in content/articles/ — yesterday's audit flagged them and nothing has removed either copy.
Category split has flattened toward politics: 22 of 58 (38%) with science down to 10 from 13, the lowest science count this week, though still above the 5/day floor.
Freshness is computed on 21 of 58 articles, a better base than yesterday's 11 of 64, and the median held at 0.1 with a max of only 1.3 days.
Al Jazeera at 12 source mentions is nearly double any other outlet today and well above its own 5 yesterday — a one-day spike driven by Middle East volume (ME rose 7 to 10), not a trend yet.
Multi-source count rose 13 to 16, the highest reading this week, while total output fell 65 to 58 — the selector traded volume for corroboration.
coverageGaps: Africa has 4 articles, all conflict or crime (Sokoto banditry, Somali piracy, Kenya amnesty) — no African economy, science or policy thread at all.
Oceania has 2 articles and both are Australia-framed (India AI compute, seaweed carbon); no Pacific island coverage for a second consecutive day.
Latin America appears only as three scattered datelines (Bogotá, Mexico City, São Sebastião) with no sustained regional story.
Science fell to 10 and leans heavily on Nature and STAT; Phys.org, Carbon Brief and Quanta contributed one article each, so the category rests on two outlets.
context: The experiment slot has now been free since 2026-05-26 and the metrics have not asked for it back — every goal has been met on consecutive audits. The open work is structural rather than parametric, and two items are outstanding for the operator: (1) the 2026-09-07 ziltivekimab pair still needs one copy removed, and (2) the dedup title-overlap layer in scripts/lib/dedup.js is gated to niche-only sources, which is why today's Quanta/New Scientist pair on the same Navier-Stokes claim republished cleanly. Ungating that layer for mainstream outlets, or adding a same-event check to scripts/validate-articles.js, would close all three duplicate shapes seen this week; both are outside the daily-tuning parameter surface and need an operator decision.
